__Bridging the gap between Data Analytics & Public Health__

While there can be uncertainty around how to use data effectively in public health, I’m here to bridge that gap.

My journey into data analytics began during my Master’s in Public Health at Columbia University, where I dove into statistical modeling, data visualization, and real-world problem solving through hands-on projects. I’ve always been drawn to how data can uncover hidden patterns, inform smarter decisions, and ultimately improve health outcomes.

I’m especially interested in using advanced analytics techniques—like predictive modeling and natural language analysis—to understand disease trends, enhance population health strategies, and support data-informed policy.

My mission is to make data science more accessible, actionable, and impactful for public health professionals everywhere.

Below, I highlight a selection of projects that demonstrate my experience in applying data science to real-world public health challenges. You can view them by navigating to the top right-hand corner.

### Data Analytics Projects

* Airbnb Rental Price prediction (Python, R): This project predicts Airbnb rental prices in New York City based on data from 2017. 

* Hot Summer Trends (R, Git): This project analyzes weather changes in Boston based on data from 2023

* COVID-19 Maps (R, GIS Tools): This project visualizes COVID-19 prevalence in NYC using maps based on data from 2010.
